info.name: P2P · Supplier Purchase Invoice (SPI)
info.description:
The Supplier Purchase Invoice flow end to end: Stage 01 supplier and PO, Stage 02 items (3-way match), Stage 03 box packaging, Stage 04 temporary put-away, close, Zoho Books, payment requests and the evidence vault.

Set `base_url` and `token` in the collection variables, then run 'login' — it stores the token for you. `spi_id`, `box_id` and `putaway_id` are filled in by the test scripts on Create Draft, Create Box and Assign; `zone_id`, `rack_id` and `shelf_id` are filled in by 'Locations — tree and recommendation'.

STAGE 04 ORDER: Set storage type → Board → Locations (counts) → Locations (tree) → Assign → then either Confirm manually, or Send for Zebra verification → Cancel → Confirm manually.

Known gap: the device callback that completes a Zebra task is not built, so that branch cannot finish yet.

request.description:
Read only — nothing is locked or reserved. Two users with the form open both see 004; whoever saves first keeps it.

This is the first call to make after migrating: it exercises auth, the tenant middleware, the branch guard, the service and the FY logic in one go.

query.description: On an EDIT only — stops the invoice counting its own quantity against itself.

request.description: Each line comes back with qty_open = po.quantity − everything already invoiced. The same service method backs the save-time guard, so the number shown is the number enforced.
Not an SPI route. The standalone flow picks a supplier directly and reuses PoLookupController.
wh_type is already a declared field on the master with exactly two values: 'Own Warehouse' and 'Third Party Warehouse'. The own/3PL split is never stored on the invoice.

What Stage 04 actually allocates against. wh_type holds 'own' or a third-party value — the own/3PL split is read from here and never stored on the invoice.

Save the id into {{warehouse_id}} for 'Set storage type'.

exec: if (first) { pm.collectionVariables.set('warehouse_id', first.id); console.log('warehouse_id =', first.id, '·', first.wh_name || first.name); }

request.description: rack_mode is the fork Stage 04 opens on: 'rack' zones own racks and shelves, 'norack' zones hold boxes directly and ARE the location.
Racks under one zone. A shelf must belong to a rack in the zone being assigned, or the assign call refuses it.

Shelves hang off their RACK — there is no /inventory/shelves/options.

A shelf has no code column of its own: its code is the rack's stored code plus the level (RC-001-SH-05).

Returns the flat 16-column row, plus `tabs` with the five counts (all / with_po / direct / with_shipment / without_shipment). The counts are unfiltered on purpose — a tab must still show its total while another tab is selected.

One query, LEFT JOINs out to the PO and through it to the shipment and opportunity.

Matches: SPI code · invoice_no · status · document_type · po.code · po.po_type · po.procurement_request_code · shipment_code · opp_code · vendor name · vendor code.

Also: type 'direct spi without po' to pull up every standalone invoice — no column holds that phrase.
Invoice + items + owns_zoho_bill + packing_summary in one call, so the detail screen makes one request rather than three.

THE FIRST WRITE OF THE WHOLE FLOW. Opening the form writes nothing — the code is allocated here, inside the transaction, under a lock on the BRANCH row.

The sequence is per branch, so a new branch starts again at 001.

purchase_order_id is null — the prototype's 'Without Purchase Order' flow. The supplier is picked directly, nothing consumes PO quantity, and THIS invoice owns its own Zoho bill.

currency_code is required when document_type is international.
Draft or mapped only. Changing purchase_order_id after items exist is refused — it would orphan every mapped line.

The WHOLE grid saves at once — never row by row, or the header totals and the lines disagree between requests.

The server computes taxable_amount, the GST split and line_total; the client never sends an amount. On an international invoice the four tax columns are written NULL, not 0 — 'does not apply' is a different fact from 'charged at zero rate'.

Response carries the recomputed packing_summary.

Refused with 422 if qty_spi exceeds what is left on the PO line.

qty_packed is DERIVED — SUM(box_items.quantity) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Nothing is stored on the item.

QA case: pack 10, delete a box of 4, confirm pending reads 4 and not 0. A missing soft-delete filter makes a removed box still count as packed.

Box and contents in ONE payload — packed quantity is summed from the contents, so a box saved without them would read as empty.

box_code is allocated by the server, sequential WITHIN the invoice (BOX-01 … BOX-n). Three SPIs packed at once never interleave.

Advanced Details (batch, expiry, serial, lot) sit on the ITEM, not the box: one carton can hold two products from two batches.

flags is an array of master ids — adding a flag is data, never a migration.

Response carries the recomputed packing_summary, so the 'remaining' table needs no second call.

Contents are replaced wholesale — a partial update would leave quantities from a product the user just removed.

The over-pack guard ignores THIS box's own current rows, or an edit could never keep its existing quantity.
Stamps sticker_printed_at and returns code_locked: true. From then on the box is never renumbered — the label is physically on a carton being scanned at put-away.

Soft delete; the quantity goes back to pending. Returns `renumbered` — the boxes after it close the gap, EXCEPT any whose sticker is already printed.

Refused when the box is already put away: it is on a shelf being scanned.

Every packed box with its contents RESOLVED: the product named, the flags read from the master, the put-away location once it has one, the sticker and the attachments.

NOT the same as 'List boxes' above. That returns the editable row shape this stage's form posts back — ids, a raw flags array, invoice-item references. This is the READ that Stage 04 Step 01 is built on: the box list, the detail panel and the products modal all come from here.
The 4x6in label as a PDF. Stamps sticker_printed_at the first time — a label in hand is a label about to go on a carton, and from then on the box is never renumbered.

Only warehouse_id is stored. putaway_mode in the response is derived from master_warehouse_master.wh_type: 'full' for our own warehouse (rack → shelf), 'summary' for a 3PL (no rack/shelf allocation).

OPEN: Stage 01 also accepts warehouse_id, so two places currently write this column.
Each row carries next_scan and ready_to_confirm, so the handheld knows what it owes without computing the chain itself.

POST, not PUT: each scan stamps its own timestamp, so it is not idempotent.

EVERY attempt is written to p2p_spi_scan_logs, success and failure alike. A rejected scan never touches the put-away row, so without that log it would be invisible.

Run this BEFORE the location scan. Expect 422 'Scan the location before the shelf.' — and then check p2p_spi_scan_logs: the row is there with result=failed, failure_reason=out_of_order and expected_scan=location.
Until confirmed_at is set the box is PICKED BUT NOT PLACED. condition_at_putaway records damage noticed AT THE RACK — a later moment than the condition recorded while unpacking in Stage 03.

item.name: Board — every box, its status and step

request.description:
Step 01's left rail in ONE read: every box of the invoice with its status (pending | draft | awaiting_scan | placed), its sub-step, its destination once assigned, and the counts behind the 0/7 PLACED bar.

Driven from the BOXES, not from the put-away rows — a box nobody has started has no put-away row at all, and that is exactly the box the operator is looking for.

status is DERIVED from confirmed_at + the location + any open task, so it cannot disagree with them.

Without `mode`, only the two numbers the opening modal asks for:

  modes.rack   — shelves available in RACKED zones
  modes.norack — active zones that hold boxes directly

Requires the invoice to have a warehouse — run 'Set storage type' first or this returns 422.

With `mode=rack|norack`, ONE call serves both halves of the screen:

  recommended — the best spot, its score and the parts that make it up
  zones[]     — zone > rack > shelf, each with its fill, used_pct, used_pct_after and eligible counts

The recommendation is the TOP OF THE SAME ranked list the tree is built from, so the two cannot disagree.

Every ineligible shelf carries a reason: inactive · in_use · no_cold_chain · no_hazardous · no_temp_control · temp_out_of_range · too_tall · full · over_weight · over_capacity.

Save the recommendation's ids into {{zone_id}}, {{rack_id}} and {{shelf_id}} — the test script below does it.

exec: console.log('recommended', rec.code, '· score', rec.score, '·', rec.used_pct + '% ->' , rec.used_pct_after + '%');
console.warn('no eligible shelf for this box ·', r.data ? r.data.eligible + '/' + r.data.total : '');

item.name: Assign a location (the box becomes a DRAFT)

request.description:
Step 02's commit, and the first write of Stage 04. ONE transaction: locks the location, RESERVES its capacity, creates the put-away row, resyncs the shelf counters and writes the activity trail.

CAPACITY IS TAKEN HERE, not at confirmation — a Zebra task can sit open for hours and the shelf must not read as free meanwhile.

Call it AGAIN with a different shelf and it is the Change button: the previous hold is released first, logged as 'reassigned' with both addresses.

409 when another operator already holds that location.
422 when the shelf is not on a rack in that zone, when the zone's rack_mode does not match, or when the box is already placed.

For a NO-RACK zone send mode=norack and leave rack_id and shelf_id out.

Step 03, Option 02. `confirmed` is the finality tick from the dialog and must be accepted — send false and it is refused with 422.

Flips the occupancy reserved -> occupied, stamps confirmed_at and verify_method=manual, and releases the lock.

THE SHELF COUNTERS DO NOT MOVE here: the space was taken at assign. What changes is who says the box is on the shelf.

Refused with 422 while a Zebra task is open on this box — cancel it first.

item.name: Send for Zebra verification — Option 01 (CREATES A SCAN TASK)

request.description:
Step 03, Option 01. Returns 201 with task_code ZT-YYYYMMDD-NNN, numbered per branch per day.

THE BOX STAYS UNPLACED: confirmed_at remains null, the row reads awaiting_scan, the capacity stays reserved, and the lock now follows the task's deadline rather than the screen's 30-minute idle timeout.

A second task on the same box is refused, and so is manual confirmation while this one is open.

exec: console.log('task', r.data.task_code, '· next scan:', r.data.next_scan, '·', r.data.scans.done + '/' + r.data.scans.required);

item.name: Tasks of this invoice (the awaiting banner)

request.description: The 'Awaiting Zebra confirmation' banner and its 0/2 scan chips, with this invoice's awaiting / placed / cancelled / expired counts.

item.name: Queue — every open task in the branch

request.description:
The Zebra Verification Tasks modal: the floor's queue ACROSS invoices, open tasks first, paginated.

Note the path — this one is not scoped to an invoice.

Closes the task and NOTHING else.

The occupancy stays RESERVED and the location stays LOCKED, because the screen reopens on the same shelf offering manual confirmation — letting the shelf go in between would hand it to somebody else mid-decision.

The box returns to draft and Option 01 is greyed as SCAN TASK CANCELLED, so the only way on is Confirm manually.

item.name: NOT BUILT — device callback (box QR then shelf QR)

request.description:
⛔ THIS ENDPOINT DOES NOT EXIST YET — it will 404.

Kept here as the known gap: the handheld's callback that verifies the box QR and then the shelf QR, and on the second one completes the task through the same confirm path as Option 02.

Until it is built the Zebra branch cannot COMPLETE — cancel then confirm manually is the only way out.

Refused while anything is unpacked: goods not in a box have no box code, so they cannot be scanned, racked or inspected.

OPEN DECISION: whether full packing should be required is not yet agreed.
Soft delete. Before the invoice goes, every line gives its quantity BACK to the PO through the fulfilment ledger — skip that and the PO stays short forever with no trace why.

Only an invoice with NO purchase order creates its own bill — with a PO the bill already exists on the order and must not be created twice.

Currently returns 501: the bill call is not written yet.
When the invoice does NOT own the bill, the response names the PO that does — rather than an empty state that reads like a failed sync.
Was an empty stub — no method, no URL, so it could not be sent. Pointed at the real endpoint; the same request also sits under '4 · Stage 03 — box packaging'.
